10 Budget Stays

heroSub: 10 hand-picked budget stays in Krabi Town that we've reviewed in depth — a social hostel by the pier, a spotless pod-bed hostel, a small boutique with big rooms, budget hotels with a pool, and stays along the Krabi River. Prices start at about ฿270–900/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest takes from real reviews at every stay
introH2: 🏙️ Budget stays in Krabi Town — what types are there, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: A lot of people assume that coming to Krabi means sleeping only at a beachfront resort on Ao Nang, but the truth is that Krabi Town (the Pak Nam area) is the most cost-effective base in the province — Chao Fah Pier for boats out to Koh Poda, Koh Kai and the Separated Sea, the night market, the walking street, and the vans heading to Ao Nang and Koh Lanta are all clustered within walking distance · So budget stays in town don't all look the same. Some are social hostels converted from an old school building, some are small boutiques with rooms bigger than the price suggests, some are budget hotels that still have a pool to cool off in, and some are stays along the Krabi River that are quieter than you'd expect · The one thing to get straight is that Krabi Town is "not on the sea." If the picture in your head is waking up and walking onto the sand, this isn't it. But if you'd rather save your room budget for boat tours and seafood, the town is the answer · This article rounds up 10 budget stays in Krabi Town that we've reviewed in depth. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices on 3 sites, and giving you direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: There are two main ways to reach Krabi · By air — land at Krabi Airport (KBV), with direct flights from Bangkok (Don Muang/Suvarnabhumi) and several major cities. From the airport into town is about 13–15 km, or roughly a 20-min drive; you can take a shared van or an airport taxi · By bus/van — there are coaches from Bangkok and southern hub cities arriving at Krabi bus station, from where you connect by songthaew into town · The stays in this article cluster in the Pak Nam area in the center of town, mostly on Maharat Road, Utarakit Road and Wachara Road, within walking distance of Chao Fah Pier, the night market, and the walking street · From town, a songthaew/van to Ao Nang Beach takes about 20–30 min, or you can take a boat from Chao Fah Pier to Railay and the islands · Grab is available in Krabi but not as dense as in Bangkok, and some areas are hard to hail from, so many stays will help call a car or offer a shuttle.

entries.name: The Chill at Krabi Hotel
entries.badge: 🌿 Highest score in the set · quiet
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pak Nam, outskirts · about 1.8 km from town
entries.addr: 121 Wachara Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Among these 10 stays, if you judge by review score, The Chill at Krabi Hotel is the one with the highest rating at 9.2 from 56 reviews on Trip.com · It's a small boutique hotel of just 37 rooms that opened in 2017, set on the Pak Nam side, an outskirts area about 1.8 km from the center of Krabi Town · True to the name The Chill, this place really sells quiet and rest rather than being right on the walking street or by the sea · Honest takes from real reviews line up on the three things people praise most: the quiet, sleep-friendly atmosphere, rooms that look cleaner and newer than the price, and the beds — one international guest even said it was the most comfortable bed of any stay they'd had across Thailand · Another highlight is the outdoor pool with a kids' pool in a tropical garden, which puts families with small children at ease, plus free private parking that suits people renting a car to get around · Staff also earn praise for being friendly and going beyond what you'd expect from a small hotel, helping call cars, book tours, and recommend places to eat and visit · Honest caveats from the reviews: this outskirts location isn't great for walking anywhere, there aren't many shops around to drop into, you mostly rely on a car, and Grab-style ride-hailing on this side isn't very reliable · On top of that the Wi-Fi signal is sometimes slow, some bathrooms have a musty smell, and the breakfast presentation and choices are still ordinary · Prices start at about ฿900/night, with an average of around ฿1,700–1,800 · Best suited to couples and families who want a quiet, budget-friendly stay with a pool and either have a private car or are ready to plan their transport, rather than people who want to step out of the room straight into markets and restaurants.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're not driving yourself, ask about the hotel's shuttle service in advance, because Grab is hard to find on the Pak Nam outskirts · And if you value a view and a sitting area, pick the Deluxe Double with Terrace, which has a balcony opening onto the garden or pool.
pros: 9.2, highest score in the set · quiet garden-house feel, sleep-friendly
Beds earn praise as a top highlight, rooms clean and looking newer than the price
Outdoor pool + kids' pool in the garden, good for families
Free private parking · friendly, helpful staff (from reviews)
cons: Outskirts location about 1.8 km from town, hard to walk anywhere, you need a car
Grab on this side isn't very reliable · Wi-Fi sometimes slow
Musty smell in some bathrooms · breakfast choices still ordinary (from reviews)

entries.name: River Front Krabi Hotel
entries.badge: 🌊 Riverside · rooms bigger than the price
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Krabi River · Utarakit Road, Pak Nam
tags: 🌊 Rooms with river and mangrove views
🛏️ Big rooms, all with a balcony
entries.addr: 299 Utarakit Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Not everyone who comes to Krabi wants to pile in together at Ao Nang. Some just want a big, clean, quiet room at a light price to use as a base for island trips — River Front Krabi Hotel is a 3-star, 40-room hotel that plays this role nicely. It sits on the Krabi River in the Pak Nam area in town, scoring 8.5 from 53 reviews on Trip.com · Front rooms look out onto the water and mangroves; back rooms open onto the pool · The point most consistently praised in real reviews is rooms that are surprisingly big and very clean — many say they're noticeably larger than the typical 3-star room, and every room has a balcony, fridge, TV and safe · The common area has a saltwater pool that's gentler on skin and eyes than heavy chlorine, surrounded by a green garden, and sometimes a troop of monkeys drops by to play in the trees around the pool, which is part of the charm of a spot by the mangroves · Staff earn praise for being friendly, especially the free tuk-tuk shuttle into town that goes a long way toward offsetting the distance · Honest caveats: this riverside location is farther from the restaurant area and the night market than some reviews make it sound, so you walk along the river for about 15–20 min or take a car into town · Breakfast costs about 200 baht extra per person and reviews disagree on the quality, sometimes lukewarm and not varied · A few reviews mention inconsistent water/plumbing in some rooms · Best suited to people who want a big, quiet riverside room on an affordable budget to use as a base for island tours and don't mind a short ride into town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you value the view, request a river-view room when you book, because the front and back rooms feel quite different · And use the free tuk-tuk shuttle into town — checking the schedule with the front desk in advance helps a lot with the location being far from restaurants.
pros: Rooms bigger than the price and very clean, all with a balcony
Rooms with river and mangrove views, quiet atmosphere
Saltwater pool with a green garden, sometimes monkeys come to play
Friendly staff, free tuk-tuk shuttle into town
cons: Location farther from the restaurant area and night market than expected
Breakfast costs about 200 baht extra/person, quality inconsistent
Plumbing/water inconsistent in some rooms (from reviews)

entries.name: City Hotel Krabi
entries.badge: 🌃 Across from the night market · lots of reviews
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krabi Town · across from the night market
tags: 🌃 Across from the night market, next to 7-Eleven
🚗 Free parking in the town center
⛴️ Walk to the pier and bus stops
entries.addr: 15/2-4 Maharat Road Soi 10, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Among these 10 stays, if you judge by number of reviews, City Hotel Krabi is the one with the most — 744 reviews on Trip.com, scoring 8.2 · It's a mid-size hotel of 105 rooms on Maharat Road Soi 10 in the Pak Nam area, opened in 1997 and with some rooms renovated again in 2021 · Its number-one selling point is location: the hotel is across from the Krabi night market and next to a 7-Eleven, which means come evening you just cross the road to find street food, sweets and souvenirs everywhere · It's a short walk to Chao Fah Pier for boats out to the islands, and within walking distance of songthaew stops and van pickup points in town — many international travelers rate the walkability here 100 out of 100 · From real reviews, the praise side is a central location within walking distance of everything, rooms that are clean and roomier than the price, free parking in the town center that's hard to find, and a 24-hour front desk that helps with late check-ins and booking boat tickets and tours · The most-mentioned honest caveat is noise — from the internal corridor, the street, and the night market in the evening — because the soundproofing isn't thick · Next is the building condition, which is starting to age in the un-renovated zones, with rust and slow drains in some rooms, few bathroom amenities, weak Wi-Fi in some spots, and no pool here · Prices start at about ฿550/night · Best suited to budget travelers, couples and families who want to stay in the center of town to use as a base for connecting cars and boats out to the islands and for strolling and eating at the night market, rather than people hunting for a pool or a sea view.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If newness matters to you, choose the Superior New Style or specifically request a renovated room · And if you're a light sleeper, ask for an inner room not facing the street or the market, because this area is lively in the evening and the soundproofing isn't thick.
pros: Across from the night market, walk to the pier and bus stops · most reviews in the set
Rooms clean and roomier than the price, comfortable beds in many rooms
Free parking in the town center that's hard to find
24-hour front desk, helps book tours, boat tickets and shuttles
cons: Soundproofing isn't thick, you hear the corridor and the street in street-facing rooms
The un-renovated zone is starting to age, rust in some rooms · few bathroom amenities
No pool · weak Wi-Fi in some spots

entries.name: Lada Krabi Residence
entries.badge: 🏙️ Town center · walk to the market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town center · Maharat Road, Pak Nam

rooms.type: Deluxe Twin Room with Balcony (~25 sqm)

tags: 🛥️ Near Chao Fah Pier, easy island trips
entries.addr: 90/71-72 Maharat Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Lada Krabi Residence is a stay for people who see Krabi as a starting point, not a destination · It's a small 2-star place (B&B / SHA Plus) on Maharat Road in the center of Krabi Town in the Pak Nam area, opened in 2012 with just 27 rooms, run as a family-managed stay that takes care of things hands-on, scoring 8.1 from 43 reviews on Trip.com and 3.9 out of 5 on TripAdvisor (#4 of 29 stays in Pak Nam) · Its number-one selling point is location — reviews most often mention being a few minutes' walk from the Krabi walking-street market that runs Friday–Sunday, and Chao Fah Pier for boats out to Koh Poda, Koh Kai and the Separated Sea is a short walk away, with the van stop to Ao Nang nearby too · From real reviews, the praise side is the central location, great value at nearly half the price of the Ao Nang beach side, rooms cleaner than expected, comfortable beds, friendly staff who help arrange tours, and breakfast included with vegetarian options that are rare at this price · Deluxe rooms have a small balcony to sit and sip coffee in the morning · The most-mentioned honest caveat is noise — the walls between rooms are fairly thin, and some nights you hear the neighboring room or the street · Next is Wi-Fi that's weak in some rooms and strongest in the lobby, a building and rooms that are starting to show their age given the opening year, and no sea and no pool here · Prices start at about ฿900/night · Best suited to budget travelers, couples and small families who focus on being out all day and coming back just to sleep, saving the difference for boat tours and seafood.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The stay has no website of its own, so book via Agoda / Booking / Trip.com and compare prices first, because they differ quite a bit at times · And if you're a light sleeper, request an upper-floor room, a corner room, or one not facing the street when you book, because the walls between rooms are fairly thin.
pros: Town-center location, walk to the walking-street market and Chao Fah Pier
Great value, nearly half the price of the Ao Nang beach side
Clean rooms, comfortable beds, balconies in Deluxe rooms
Friendly staff, help arrange island tours · breakfast included with vegetarian options
cons: Walls between rooms are fairly thin, you hear the neighboring room
Wi-Fi weak in some rooms, strongest in the lobby
No sea, no pool · building starting to show its age (opened 2012)

entries.name: Sleep Whale Hotel
entries.badge: 🏊 Budget but with a pool · renovated 2023
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krabi Town · Maharat Road, Pak Nam

rooms.type: Balcony Double Room, city view (~27 sqm)

tags: 🏔️ Many rooms with a mountain-view balcony
entries.addr: 23 Maharat Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Sleep Whale Hotel is a hotel for people looking for a budget stay in Krabi Town that still has a pool, which is a combination you don't find often, since most budget hotels in the town center have no pool · It's a small boutique hotel of just 35 rooms on Maharat Road in the Pak Nam area, opened in 2013 and freshly renovated in 2023, which makes the rooms look newer and fresher than many budget hotels in town, scoring 8.9 from 172 reviews on Trip.com · The selling point that sets it apart is an outdoor pool with a separate kids' pool, to cool off after a full day of walking around, good for families with small children · Most rooms are about 27 sqm, larger than the standard room of a typical budget hotel, and many have a balcony, with some looking out onto Krabi's limestone mountains as a backdrop · Reviews consistently praise that rooms are very clean, bathrooms roomy, staff friendly and helpful both morning and late, and there's free parking · The most-mentioned honest caveat is that the walls and floors are fairly thin, so some nights you hear the neighboring room, the corridor and the street · Next is a location outside the town center, about 1.5–2 km from the commercial area and the Chao Fah night market — walkable, but about 20–30 min, so many people choose to take a car or rent a motorbike into town · Breakfast is simple with limited and repeated choices, and service is inconsistent in some cases · Prices start at about ฿700/night · Best suited to budget travelers, families with kids, and people driving themselves who want to stay in town but still want a pool, rather than people hunting for a beachfront resort or a location right by the market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room not next to the main corridor or facing the street, because the walls and floors are fairly thin · And the hotel is outside the town center, a far 20–30 min walk to the night market, so renting a motorbike at the front desk or calling a car is more convenient.
pros: A pool + kids' pool at a budget hotel in the town center, hard to find at this price
Rooms about 27 sqm, clean and looking new after the 2023 renovation
Many rooms with a balcony and mountain views · roomy bathrooms
Friendly, helpful staff both morning and late · free parking
cons: Walls and floors are fairly thin, you hear the neighboring room and corridor
Outside the town center, you walk 20–30 min or take a car to the market
Limited and repeated breakfast choices · inconsistent service in some cases

entries.name: Krabi Golden Hill Hotel
entries.badge: 🤫 Quiet on a hill · with a pool
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pak Nam, on a hill · about 1 km from town
tags: 🪟 Every room has a private balcony
entries.addr: 18 Chamai Anusorn Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Krabi Golden Hill Hotel is a hotel for people who want a budget stay that still has a pool and quiet in Krabi, without paying beachfront-resort prices · It's a small 3-star hotel of about 44 rooms on a hill on Chamai Anusorn Road in the Pak Nam area, only about 1 km from the center of Krabi Town, opened in 2008, with every room having a private balcony, scoring 8.1 from 16 reviews on Trip.com · Its position on a hill and off the main road makes the surroundings quieter than a stay in the middle of the market, which people who sleep easily and like calm will really appreciate · From real reviews, the praise side is a clean pool at a budget price that's hard to find, rooms cleaner and roomier than expected, comfortable beds, a private balcony in every room, friendly and helpful staff, a quiet atmosphere good for resting, and free parking plus an EV charger that's still rare at budget hotels · The most-mentioned honest caveat is the hilltop position fairly far from shops and restaurants — there are no shops right at the door, so you call a car or walk about 15–20 min into town, and the shuttle service into town isn't always on time · Next is air-con that's noisy enough to vibrate in some rooms, decor and furniture starting to age given the 2008 building, and limited breakfast choices · It must be said honestly that the number of reviews on Trip.com is still small (16 reviews), so read the latest reviews alongside this before deciding · Prices start at about ฿700/night · Best suited to budget travelers who still want a pool and quiet, couples who value privacy, and families driving themselves.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Transport is the thing to plan most, because the hotel is on a hill about 1 km from town and there are no shops at the door, so if you don't have a car, be ready to call a Grab/motorbike taxi · And if room condition matters to you, choose a Deluxe and request the most recently maintained room.
pros: A pool at a budget price, which is hard to find in Krabi
Rooms cleaner and roomier than expected, every room has a private balcony
Quiet atmosphere good for resting, about 1 km from town
Free parking and an EV charger, good for people driving themselves
cons: On a hill far from shops, you handle getting into town yourself · shuttle not always on time
Air-con noisy enough to vibrate in some rooms · building starting to age (opened 2008)
Limited breakfast choices · still few online reviews (16 reviews)

entries.name: K.L. Boutique Hotel
entries.badge: 🛏️ Rooms bigger than the price · cool design
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krabi Town · Maharat Road Soi 2, Pak Nam
tags: ⛴️ Walk to the pier and night market
entries.addr: 32 Maharat Road Soi 2, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Some people come to Krabi not hunting for a beachfront resort costing thousands a night, but just wanting a small, clean stay with a big room at a light price in the center of town — K.L. Boutique Hotel is a name independent budget travelers mention often in Krabi Town · It's a small boutique hotel of just 14 rooms on Maharat Road Soi 2 in the Pak Nam area, renovated in 2020, scoring 9.1 from 31 reviews on Trip.com and 4.6 out of 5 on TripAdvisor (#8 of 171 specialty-lodging stays in Krabi) · The point real reviews praise most consistently is rooms that are big and very clean for the price — many say they're noticeably larger than stays at the same price in town — and the contemporary industrial decor that many reviews say is cooler than the exterior suggests, a raw-concrete tone mixed with wood and steel · Location is also a strength: international reviews rate the walkability high at about 98 out of 100, a roughly 10-min walk to Chao Fah Pier for boats out to the islands and to the walking street, and near the night market · There's free parking in the town center that's hard to find, and many reviews mention the gentleman at the front desk who looks after guests almost constantly and helps book tours and boat tickets · The most-mentioned honest caveat is no elevator — you climb the stairs, which is tough when hauling a big suitcase · Next is doors that close loudly and echoes in the corridor when guests in other rooms come back late, occasional insects as you'd find at a small stay in the tropics, no pool, and a light breakfast of toast, tea and coffee · Prices start at about ฿450/night (it's been reported as low as around 400 baht in low season) · Best suited to budget travelers, couples and solo travelers who want a big, clean, well-designed room within walking distance of everything in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no elevator here, so if you have a big suitcase, are traveling with elderly companions, or don't want to haul things up the stairs, ask for a ground-floor room when you book · And breakfast is light, so walk out to eat at the nearby markets and town restaurants, where food is cheaper and more varied.
pros: Rooms bigger than the price and very clean, industrial design cooler than the exterior
Town-center location, walk to the pier, night market and walking street
Owner and staff are friendly, help book tours and boat tickets
Free parking in the town center that's hard to find · 9.1 score + TripAdvisor 4.6
cons: No elevator, you climb the stairs, which is tough when hauling luggage
Loud doors and echoes in the corridor when guests return late
No pool · light breakfast · occasional insects (from reviews)

entries.name: Hogwortz Hostel
tags: 🛏️ Pod beds with curtains + big lockers
✨ Reviews praise the cleanliness again and again
entries.addr: 2/7 Maharat Road Soi 10, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Hogwortz Hostel is a small hostel in the center of Krabi Town that suits budget travelers who value cleanliness and sleep over partying · It's named as a play on the wizarding school in Harry Potter, but in reality the theme is just a light touch — there are name signs, cardboard character cutouts, and on some nights a movie plays in the common corner. Anyone expecting a full wizard-castle atmosphere may feel they got less than imagined · It's on Maharat Road Soi 10 in the Pak Nam area, opened around 2015, scoring 8.9 from 449 reviews on Trip.com and 4 out of 5 on TripAdvisor · The real heart is the pod-style dorm beds in 6–8-bed rooms, both mixed and female-only, each bed with a privacy curtain, reading light, power outlet, and a big locker for valuables. A point many people especially praise is that the upper beds use a staircase instead of the thin metal ladder of a typical hostel, making it easier and safer to climb up and down · The thing praised again and again, and the main reason people come back with good reviews, is the cleanliness — many use the phrase clean as new · Location is also a strength: about a 3-min walk to the walking street and night market, and a few more minutes to Chao Fah Pier for boats out to the islands · The most-mentioned honest caveat is that the beds are fairly firm — one side-sleeper review said they couldn't sleep well · Next is small, shared bathrooms with a wait at busy times, with the top-floor bathroom not as clean as the lower floors, air-con on a timer, weak Wi-Fi upstairs, a multi-floor building with no elevator, no pool, and a deposit of about 300 baht per person refunded at checkout · Dorm beds start at about ฿270/night · Best suited to solo travelers, backpacking pairs, and people using Krabi as a stopover before heading to the islands, rather than large families or people who want hotel-level convenience.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bring cash for the roughly 300-baht-per-person deposit refunded at checkout · If you like a soft mattress, accept that the beds are fairly firm and maybe pack an extra layer or pillow · And if you need to work online, choose a lower-floor bed where the Wi-Fi is stronger.
pros: Reviews praise the cleanliness again and again, rooms tidy as new · lots of reviews, 449
Pod beds with a privacy curtain, big locker, reading light
Quiet, good for people who actually want to sleep, not the party crowd
Town-center location, 3-min walk to the night market · near Chao Fah Pier
cons: Beds are fairly firm, people who like a soft mattress may need to adjust
Small, shared bathrooms, a wait at busy times · no pool
Multi-floor building with no elevator · about a 300-baht/person deposit (refunded at checkout)

entries.type: 2-Star Hostel in a Former Cinema · Box Rooms
entries.name: Holiday Station Hostel
entries.badge: 🎬 Box rooms in a former cinema · good value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krabi Town · Utarakit Road, Pak Nam
tags: 🎬 Renovated from a former cinema building
entries.addr: 251/1 Utarakit Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: Holiday Station Hostel is a budget stay in the center of Krabi Town that suits travelers on a tight budget who want more privacy than an open-bed dorm but don't want to pay hotel prices yet · The thing that makes this place easy to remember and fun to retell is the building: it was renovated from a former cinema that had stopped showing films in Krabi Town, so the owner took the large hall space and divided it into many small rooms, becoming capsule-style box rooms that many people compare to budget stays in Japan · It's on Utarakit Road in the Pak Nam area in the center of town, scoring around 8.6 from several hundred reviews by real guests, and 4 out of 5 on TripAdvisor · From real reviews, the praise raised most often is the value — many are surprised they pay just a few hundred baht a night yet get a private, enclosed room that's clean · Next is the town-center location within walking distance of the walking street, the night market and the Black Crab statue, and not far from Chao Fah Pier, with a 24-hour reception that's an advantage over many small hostels, plus attention to small details like leaving drinking water and toilet paper outside the room · The most-mentioned honest caveat is thin walls — in some rooms the walls don't go all the way to the ceiling, so you hear the neighboring room fairly clearly · Next is Wi-Fi that's weak and unstable even in the common area, which is complained about repeatedly, some box rooms where you can't adjust the air-con yourself, bathroom cleanliness at some times, inconsistent reception, and no pool and no breakfast here · Prices start at about ฿420/night (cheaper in low season) · Best suited to solo travelers, budget couples, and people who want a private enclosed room at a price close to a dorm, using Krabi Town as a base for island trips.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Prepare for noise, because the box rooms are partitioned in the hall of the former cinema and some walls don't go all the way to the ceiling, so if you're sensitive to noise, pack earplugs · And if you have to work online, don't rely on the stay's Wi-Fi alone — bring a mobile data SIM as a backup plan.
pros: Great value on a few-hundred-baht budget, a private enclosed room that's clean · lots of reviews
Town-center location, walk to the night market, walking street and Black Crab statue
24-hour reception, you can check in even arriving late or on an evening flight
A box-room-in-a-former-cinema concept that's novel and memorable
cons: Thin walls, you hear the neighboring room fairly clearly
Wi-Fi weak and unstable, even in the common area
No pool, no breakfast · some box rooms can't adjust the air-con yourself

entries.name: Pak-Up Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krabi Town · Utarakit Road · next to Chao Fah Pier
entries.addr: 87 Utarakit Road, Pak Nam, Mueang District, Krabi
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Krabi alone and want to meet new friends, not just find somewhere to crash, Pak-Up Hostel is the name backpackers mention most in Krabi Town · It's a full-on social hostel designed to turn strangers into friends within one night, opened in 2010 in a former primary-school building, with each dorm named after a school subject or an artist, like Art, English or Picasso, scoring 8.8 from 175 reviews on Trip.com, and it has won Krabi's most popular hostel at Hostelworld's Hoscars three years running · The heart is the big, sturdy wooden bunk beds built into the structure, not the thin metal beds that rock the whole room when the person above turns over. Every bed has a privacy curtain that fully closes, a reading light, its own outlet and USB port, and a big locker under the bed · What sets it apart from quiet hostels is the common area — there's a bar that almost every night has activities from pub quiz, beer pong and bingo to a Pub Crawl out to the bars in the Ao Nang area about 3 nights a week, plus a small pool to cool off in and a functional gym on the rooftop with a city view · Location is also a strength: just about a 1-min walk to Chao Fah Pier for boats out to the islands, and near the night market and bus stops · The most-mentioned honest caveat is noise — it's a social hostel with parties, and on activity nights the noise bounces around until late, especially the rooms near the bar · Next is no sea, so you take a car to Ao Nang for about 20–25 min, a simple free breakfast that's not a buffet, some wooden beds that creak, slow bar service when it's busy, and a 4-floor building with no elevator · Dorm beds start at about ฿270/night · Best suited to solo travelers, backpacking pairs, and travelers who want a social atmosphere, a town-center location, and dorm beds that are genuinely good, rather than families with small children or people hunting for quiet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a bed in an upper-floor dorm away from the bar, because on party or Pub Crawl nights the noise bounces around until late — keeping earplugs on hand helps a lot · And if you're set on island trips, you can book a tour through reception, because it's a one-minute walk from the stay to the boats at Chao Fah Pier.
pros: Town-center location, 1-min walk to Chao Fah Pier, easiest island access in the set
Steady wooden bunk beds with a privacy curtain and a big locker
Social atmosphere, easy to meet new friends, with a pool, bar and rooftop gym
Friendly staff, help arrange island tours · great value on a backpacker budget
cons: On party nights it's loud until late, rooms near the bar are hard to sleep in
No sea, about a 20–25 min drive from Ao Nang Beach · simple breakfast
4-floor building with no elevator · some wooden beds creak

advice.bodyHtml: → The Chill at Krabi Hotel ฿900, 9.2 the highest score in the set, a quiet garden-house feel, a pool, beds that earn praise, good for people with a car

advice.head: On a budget but still want a pool
advice.bodyHtml: → Sleep Whale Hotel ฿700, new rooms renovated in 2023, a pool + kids' pool · or Krabi Golden Hill Hotel ฿700, a pool, quiet on a hill + EV charging

advice.head: Want a big private room, good design, light budget
advice.bodyHtml: → K.L. Boutique Hotel ฿450, a small boutique of 14 rooms, rooms bigger than the price, industrial design, walk to the pier, 9.1 score

advice.head: Traveling solo, want to meet new friends
advice.bodyHtml: → Pak-Up Hostel ฿270, social, with a pool, bar and rooftop gym, 1-min walk to Chao Fah Pier, easiest island access

advice.head: Lowest budget, but want cleanliness and quiet
advice.bodyHtml: → Hogwortz Hostel ฿270, pod beds with curtains, big lockers, reviews praise the cleanliness, quieter than party hostels

advice.head: Want to walk to the night market and the pier
advice.bodyHtml: → City Hotel Krabi ฿550, across from the night market, free parking, 24-hr front desk · or Lada Krabi Residence ฿900, walk to the walking-street market

advice.head: Want a big riverside room, quieter than the town center
advice.bodyHtml: → River Front Krabi Hotel ฿900, on the Krabi River, big rooms all with a balcony, a saltwater pool, a free tuk-tuk shuttle into town

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room price range (hostels are per dorm bed) and may change with the date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms; we did not stay ourselves · All the stays are in Krabi Town (the Pak Nam area), which is the town center, not on the sea, suited to use as a base for boats out to the islands and connecting cars to Ao Nang/Koh Lanta · Many of the stays have no pool and some have no elevator, so read the details of each before booking · During Krabi's high season (November–April) prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so small stays should be booked 2–4 weeks ahead or more · Grab is available in Krabi but hard to hail in some areas, so many stays will help call a car or offer a shuttle · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about budget stays in Krabi Town

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best budget stay in Krabi Town?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style · If you judge by score, The Chill at Krabi Hotel has 9.2, the highest in the set, quiet with a pool (but it's on the outskirts and you need a car) · If you want a big, well-designed private room on a light budget, K.L. Boutique Hotel scores 9.1 from ฿450 · If you're traveling solo and want to meet friends, Pak-Up Hostel from ฿270 is social and next to the pier · If you're on a budget but want a pool, Sleep Whale Hotel from ฿700 · And if you want to walk to the night market, City Hotel Krabi from ฿550

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays in Krabi Town cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿270–900 per night · The cheapest are the dorm beds at Pak-Up Hostel and Hogwortz Hostel from ฿270 · Light-budget private rooms start at K.L. Boutique Hotel ฿450 and Holiday Station Hostel ฿420 · The budget hotels with a pool are Sleep Whale and Krabi Golden Hill from ฿700 · And the 3-star hotels like The Chill and River Front start at ฿900 · All prices are approximate starting prices, and during high season prices may run higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Is it better to stay in Krabi Town or in Ao Nang?
faq.a: Krabi Town (Pak Nam) isn't on the sea, but it's a transport base — walk to Chao Fah Pier for boats out to the islands, the night market, the walking street, and the bus stops, with room and food costs cheaper than the beach side, suited to people who go out to the islands all day and come back to sleep · Ao Nang is on the beach, suited to people who want to wake up and walk onto the sea and spend time on the sand, but starting prices are usually higher · All 10 stays in this article are in town, better suited to use as a base for trips than to relax by the beach

faq.q: ❓ Which budget stays in Krabi Town have a pool?
faq.a: Only a few still have a pool at a budget price · The Chill at Krabi Hotel has an outdoor pool + kids' pool (outskirts) · River Front Krabi Hotel has a saltwater pool by the river · Sleep Whale Hotel has a pool + kids' pool in town · Krabi Golden Hill Hotel has a small pool on a hill · and Pak-Up Hostel has a small pool to cool off in · As for City Hotel, Lada, K.L. Boutique, Hogwortz and Holiday Station, they have no pool

faq.q: ❓ Traveling Krabi solo/backpacking, which hostel should I stay at?
faq.a: There are 3 hostels in this set with different personalities · Pak-Up Hostel from ฿270 is social, with a bar, pool, rooftop gym and nightly activities, a 1-min walk to the pier, good for people who want to meet friends · Hogwortz Hostel from ฿270 focuses on clean, quiet pod beds, good for people who value sleep over partying · Holiday Station Hostel from ฿420 has private enclosed box rooms in a former cinema building, good for people who want an enclosed room at a price close to a dorm

faq.q: ❓ How far in advance should I book a stay in Krabi Town?
faq.a: Most of the stays in this article are small (14–105 rooms, some just 14 rooms), so they fill fast · During high season (November–April), book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, especially small stays like K.L. Boutique (14 rooms) and the good dorm beds at Pak-Up and Hogwortz · In other periods 1–2 weeks is enough · Most platforms usually offer Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in that kind of rate first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com to get the best price
